questions.question: When transporting explosives, what must you have?
questions.explanation: You must follow a written route plan when transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives. Avoid heavily populated areas, crowds, tunnels, narrow streets, and alleys. Check for any route restrictions before you travel.

questions.question: Many poisonous products are also:
questions.explanation: Many hazardous materials that are poisonous are also flammable.

questions.question: When can you drive a vehicle that is not properly placarded?

options.text: To make room for other vehicles.
If you are traveling fewer than 10 miles.

questions.explanation: A vehicle that is not properly placarded can only be driven when necessary to protect life or property in an emergency.

questions.question: What license do you need to transport hazardous materials?

options.text: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement
A CDL with a tank endorsement
A CDL with a cargo endorsement

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement
questions.explanation: You need a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle used to transport hazardous materials.

questions.question: What must you have in your vehicle when transporting chlorine?
questions.explanation: You must carry an approved gas mask in your vehicle when transporting chlorine in cargo tanks.

questions.question: Where should you keep shipping papers while driving?
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's side door or in another location where you can easily reach them while wearing your seat belt. The papers must be easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: What should you check before transporting hazardous materials?

options.text: That shipping papers match the markings and labels on packages.
That shipping papers are written in code.
That all packages are labeled as poison.

questions.correctAnswerText: That shipping papers match the markings and labels on packages.
questions.explanation: Compare package markings and labels to the shipping papers. Make sure the shipper has listed the correct information and applied the proper labels to all packages.

questions.question: What is important to know about radioactive material packages?

options.text: Radiation passes through packages and affects nearby packages.
The package must be transported in the cab.
The package should be loaded on its side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation passes through packages and affects nearby packages.
questions.explanation: Radiation passes through each radioactive package and affects all nearby packages. There are limits on how many packages can be loaded together.

questions.question: If "G" appears in Column 1 of a shipping paper, what else must be listed?

options.text: The technical name of the hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: The technical name of the hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: A "G" in Column 1 means Column 2 contains a generic name. Generic names must be accompanied by the technical name of the material.

questions.question: Who can transport hazardous materials?

options.text: A driver with a CDL and hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver with a CDL and hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: You need a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to operate any vehicle used to transport hazardous materials.

questions.question: What should you NOT use when loading hazardous materials containers?
questions.explanation: Protect hazardous materials containers. Do not use hooks because they can damage containers or packaging.

questions.question: If your hazardous materials cargo catches fire, what should you do?

options.text: Try to put it out with a fire extinguisher
Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire
Wait for the fire to go out on its own

questions.correctAnswerText: Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials fires need special training and gear. Do not try to fight the fire yourself unless you are trained and equipped.

questions.question: What symbol shows a material is a marine pollutant?

options.text: A bird inside a red octagon
A fish inside a white triangle with an X through it
A light blue square with a dark blue X through it

questions.correctAnswerText: A fish inside a white triangle with an X through it
questions.explanation: The marine pollutant symbol is a fish inside a white triangle with an X through it.

questions.question: If hazardous materials are leaking and you have no phone, what should you do?

options.text: Drive to a hazardous materials cleanup facility
Send someone else to get help

questions.correctAnswerText: Send someone else to get help
questions.explanation: If hazardous materials leak, do not drive. Park your vehicle, secure it, stay with it, and get help. If you have no phone, send someone else for help. Driving spreads contamination over a larger area.

questions.question: How many identical placards must be on a vehicle?
questions.explanation: A vehicle carrying hazardous materials must have at least four identical placards: one on the front, one on the back, and one on each side.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with empty hazardous materials tanks, what must you do at a railroad crossing?

options.text: You do not need to cross
You must slow down but do not have to stop

questions.explanation: If your vehicle has hazardous materials tanks, you must stop at railroad crossings. This applies whether the tanks are full or empty.

questions.question: Which is NOT your job as a driver at an accident scene?

options.text: Keep people away from the scene
Fight the fire on your own
Tell emergency personnel about the hazardous materials

questions.correctAnswerText: Fight the fire on your own
questions.explanation: As a driver, keep people away, limit material spread if safe, and inform emergency personnel of the dangers. Do not fight hazardous materials fires unless you have proper equipment and training.

questions.question: What should you do before opening trailer doors during a fire?

options.text: Feel the doors to check if they are hot

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel the doors to check if they are hot
questions.explanation: Always feel the doors first. If they are hot, there may be a cargo fire inside. Do not open hot doors because fresh air can make the fire worse.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1 explosives, you must park at least ____ away from any building.
questions.explanation: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, keep 300 feet away from buildings, bridges, tunnels, gathering places, and open fires.

questions.question: When can you leave a vehicle carrying explosives unattended?

options.text: On the shoulder of a highway

questions.explanation: You may only leave your vehicle unattended in a safe haven. A safe haven is an approved location for parking vehicles loaded with explosives.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, the liquid discharge valves should be:
questions.explanation: On a compressed gas tank, liquid discharge valves must be opened during loading and unloading. At all other times, they must be kept closed.

questions.question: Where should a placard be placed?

options.text: At least three inches away from any other markings.
Under a ladder, if space is limited.
On a background that matches the placard color.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least three inches away from any other markings.
questions.explanation: A placard must be at least three inches away from any other markings. Keep it clear of doors and ladders. Always place the placard against a background color that is different from the placard.

questions.question: Where can you find identification numbers for chemicals?

options.text: In the DOT Emergency Response Guide.
In the Periodic Table of Elements.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the DOT Emergency Response Guide.
questions.explanation: The DOT Emergency Response Guide (ERG) contains information about hazardous chemicals. It is organized by the proper shipping names and identification numbers of materials.

questions.question: On shipping papers, the identification number, shipping name, and hazard class should:

options.text: Be shortened if using small paper.
Be shortened only if the shortened forms are clear.

questions.explanation: On hazardous materials shipping papers, the identification number, shipping name, and hazard class must not be shortened, unless the regulations specifically allow it.

questions.question: Before opening trailer doors during a truck fire, what should you do?

options.text: Feel the doors to see if they are hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel the doors to see if they are hot.
questions.explanation: Before opening trailer doors during a fire, feel them to check if they are hot. Hot doors mean there may be a cargo fire inside. If the doors are hot, keep them closed.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1 explosives, how far must you park from the nearest building?
questions.explanation: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, do not park within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. The only exception is if you park for a short time for an operational need, such as refueling.

questions.question: If a shipping paper has both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, the hazardous materials may need to be:

options.text: Circled with a pen or marker.

questions.explanation: If a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, the hazardous materials must be set apart in one of three ways: listed first, highlighted in a contrasting color, or marked with an "X" in an "HM" column.

questions.question: If a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, what must you do?

options.text: Write the hazardous materials in red ink.

questions.explanation: When a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, the hazardous materials must be entered first.

questions.question: Who is responsible for labeling hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for packaging, marking, and labeling hazardous materials correctly. The driver should check that all materials are properly labeled.

questions.question: Where must hazardous materials placards be placed?

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the outside of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed on the front, rear, and both sides of a vehicle.
